name: Hariph
overview: Hariph was a male leader identified as a non-Levite in the book of Nehemiah. He is noted for his role as one of the signatories on the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, his inclusion among the leaders highlights his recognized authority during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Hariph means 'one born at harvest time,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with agricultural imagery. This meaning is noted in Nehemiah 10:19 and provides a cultural context for his personal identity without indicating divine naming.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hariph was a descendant of Jacob, establishing his Israelite heritage. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hariph's significance lies in his role as a non-Levite leader who pledged commitment to the covenant renewal community following the exile. His inclusion among the sealed signatories in Nehemiah 10:19 demonstrates his participation in the collective dedication to uphold God's law, marking him as a key figure in the restoration of Israel's covenant faithfulness.
